subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed `sessions_spawn` keep returning `accepted` and then surface a typed/logged terminal startup failure asynchronously, or should it preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning?
rationale: The choice changes the public async spawn contract, registry/session state semantics, and the overlap with the broader lifecycle-event work, so a maintainer should choose before another automated implementation attempt.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failures
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make sandbox startup failures visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox initialization before the accepted response to fail fast, accepting extra latency and compatibility review for existing callers.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Leave this sandbox-specific issue open while maintainers settle the broader lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failures
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and make sandbox startup failures visible as typed terminal state in logs, session history, subagent status, and waits.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame across the central spawn/sandbox/gateway paths points to Vincent Koc, making him the best available routing owner for the contract decision.
